subject: High latency & error spikes — Dedicated pool saturation (Fintegrate)
messages:
From: Samantha Lee <samantha.lee@fintegrate.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement <procurement@fintegrate.com>, Brian Cole <brian.cole@fintegrate.com>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:15:22 -0700
Subject: Re: production incidents — urgent

Marissa,

We're seeing a significant degradation in the last 60 minutes across multiple endpoints in production: p95 latency jumped from ~220ms to ~1.2s, error rate for /generate is ~4.8% (baseline ~0.6%), and overall throughput is falling despite steady request volume. Our on-call flagged repeated 503s and long tails. This is impacting customer-facing flows (loan approvals).

Can you confirm whether this is a transient warm-up or something on your side? We have reserved capacity with Redwood (dedicated GPU pool) — this looks like the pool has saturated. We need immediate mitigation and an ETA for resolution.

I've attached a quick metrics screenshot from our side.

Thanks,
Samantha
Samantha Lee
Head of Engineering, Fintegrate

Subject: Re: production incidents — urgent

Samantha — thanks for the flag and the screenshot. We're taking this seriously and I’m standing up a bridge now. I’ve looped in engineering (Vivek), CS (Evelyn) and Sales Ops (Rishi).

Quick answers: we are seeing elevated token processing in a subset of your routes which is saturating the dedicated pool for your reserved capacity. Initial plan is: 1) enable an immediate fallback to the quantized model variant for non-critical routes, 2) increase burst capacity for your pool while we investigate root cause, and 3) throttle very long-context jobs that are monopolizing batching. I’ll confirm actions on the bridge in the next 10 minutes.

I attached our baseline SLA report for context and will share the bridge link.

—Marissa
Director, Customer Success | Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:27:05 -0700
Subject: ACTION: Fintegrate dedicated pool saturated — need immediate mitigations

Team — on escalation from Fintegrate (customer, DEAL-9482). Key facts:
- Customer observes p95 ~1.2s, error spikes ~4.8%, throughput drop; incidents began ~08:45 PDT.
- They are on reserved capacity in us-west with a dedicated GPU pool (pinned instances).
- Early signs: a small set of long-context batch jobs and a rise in streaming sessions that increased average sequence length.

Immediate asks (please acknowledge):
1) Engineering (Vivek): can you open the pool to short-term bursting (+15%) and enable the quantized fallback on non-critical endpoints? Impact/risk?
2) CS (Evelyn): communicate the short-term mitigation to the customer and confirm which routes are safe for degraded model variants.
3) Sales/Ops (Rishi): prepare a short note on credits / SLA protection if we breach the committed throughput; capture any procurement concerns from their cc.

We need a 30-min triage then an executive summary for Fintegrate’s VP and our leadership. I’ll draft the MAP (mutual action plan).

—Marissa
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn.hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Hannah Schmitt <hannah.schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Jun 2025 09:41:12 -0700
Subject: Re: ACTION: Fintegrate dedicated pool saturated — need immediate mitigations

On Tue, Jun 24, 2025 at 09:27, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai> wrote:
> Team — on escalation from Fintegrate (customer, DEAL-9482). Key facts:

I’ve pulled the serving metrics and traces. Preliminary root cause: a combination of (a) several long-context inference jobs that dramatically increased average tokens per request, and (b) continuous batching reaching the max tokens/second configured for the dedicated pool. The scheduler is hitting the throughput cap and requests are queuing — hence the p95 tails and 503s.

Immediate actions I enacted (now):
- Opened burst capacity by 15% for the Fintegrate pool (temporary, 2h window).
- Enabled quantized model variant for the non-sensitive endpoints for this customer (rollback safe).
- Added a short-term rate-limit on requests with sequence_length > 4096 for the pool (soft 429 responses with guidance).

Estimated customer impact: should reduce p95 to ~300–450ms for critical routes and bring error rate back to ~0.8% within 8–12 minutes. Risk: quantized variant may have subtle quality regressions on very long prompts — documented in the MAP.

Next steps: we should schedule a follow-up patch (hours) to rebalance batch size and tune kernel selection; later (days) a capacity increase or re-provisioning if their workload pattern persists. I’ll dump the exact commands and config diffs to the incident doc.

—Vivek
Head of Serving Runtime, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: production incidents — urgent

Samantha — quick update for you:
- We enabled a temporary 15% burst on your dedicated pool.
- We switched non-sensitive routes to the quantized fallback (degraded variant) to avoid queuing.
- We applied a soft throttle for requests with sequence length >4096.

We expect improved latency within ~10 minutes; Vivek estimates p95 down to 300–450ms for critical routes. We are preparing a formal mutual action plan and will follow up with a short customer-friendly incident summary and any applicable credits.

I’ll keep you posted on the MAP and next steps.

Best,
Rishi
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Thu, 26 Jun 2025 18:42:00 -0700
Subject: FIN: Executive memo and next steps for Fintegrate incident

Marissa — short note after the post-mortem:
- Incident window: 2025-06-24T08:45:00-07:00 to 2025-06-24T10:05:00-07:00. Root cause: dedicated pool throughput cap reached due to increased tokens/sec from long-context jobs.
- Mitigations applied: +15% burst, quantized fallbacks on non-critical routes, sequence-length soft throttle.
- Business impact: transient user-facing latency and increased error rate; no data loss. We estimate customer-facing availability hit of ~1.2% for the window.

Action items for execs & commercial:
1) Offer a one-time credit aligned to SLA terms (Rishi to propose amount).
2) Ops: consider increasing reserved capacity or adding a larger instance class for Fintegrate if their traffic profile is persistent.
3) Product: evaluate auto-detection of long-context job patterns and proactive re-routing to optimized pools.

I’ll draft a 1-page executive memo for Legal/Revenue and forward it to leadership by tomorrow morning.

—Hannah
Senior Programs Manager, Customer Reliability
